messages.content:
The workspace contains `perf.py` — a module whose functions are CORRECT but
too slow for production. Your job: make every function fast enough to pass
the timing budgets below while keeping the results identical.

Functions and their required behavior (unchanged):

- `common_elements(a, b)` — sorted list of values appearing in both lists
- `fib(n)` — nth Fibonacci number (fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1)
- `count_pairs(nums, target)` — number of index pairs i<j with
  nums[i]+nums[j] == target
- `dedupe_keep_order(items)` — remove duplicates, preserving first-seen order

Timing budgets (generous — any reasonable algorithmic fix sails through):
- `common_elements` on two 200,000-element lists: under 2 seconds
- `fib(300)`: under 2 seconds
- `count_pairs` on 100,000 elements: under 2 seconds
- `dedupe_keep_order` on 200,000 items: under 2 seconds

Rules: keep the function names and signatures; standard library only; the
module must still import cleanly. Correctness is tested with exact expected
values — optimize the algorithms, don't approximate.

text:
Done. `perf.py` rewritten with the same names/signatures, stdlib only.

| function | change | measured (target < 2s) |
|---|---|---|
| `common_elements` | O(n·m) scans → `sorted(set(a) & set(b))` | 0.025s @ 200k×200k |
| `fib` | exponential recursion → iterative loop | 0.000011s @ n=300 |
| `count_pairs` | O(n²) double loop → single pass with a complement counter | 0.006s @ 100k |
| `dedupe_keep_order` | O(n²) list scans → `list(dict.fromkeys(items))` | 0.007s @ 200k |

Correctness verified against the original implementations: 200 randomized trials each for `common_elements` / `count_pairs` / `dedupe_keep_order`, `fib(0..59)` plus `fib(300)` against a memoized reference — all exact matches.

Two of the fast paths require hashable values, which the originals did not, so `common_elements` and `dedupe_keep_order` catch `TypeError` and fall back to the original scan (verified with list-of-list inputs). The `count_pairs` counter approach handles duplicate values correctly — it counts occurrences of the complement seen so far rather than deduping.

One leftover: my scratch test file is at `C:\Users\bghur\AppData\Local\Temp\perftest.py`; the sandbox blocked deleting outside the working dirs, so it's still there.
